summary: Michael Viggo Fausbøll was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his Cand.theol. at the University of Copenhagen (1838–1847) studying under Niels Ludvig Westergaard, where he later served as assistant librarian (1861) and Professor of Indian Philology (1878–1902).

Michael W. Meister is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Harvard University (B.A. ~1960–1964, M.A. ~1969–1971, Ph.D. ~1971–1974) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1967–1968), where he became a professor around 1976.

Michael Weiers was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. After completing his dissertation at the University of Bonn (~1960–1965), he served there as a professor from 1972 to 2003 and became an honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University (~1989).

Michael Wenger is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He earned an M.A. at The New School and trained under Mel Weitsman (~1972–2021). He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at the San Francisco Zen Center (~1984–2012) and founded Dragons Leap Meditation Center.

Michael Willis is an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Victoria under Siri Gunasinghe and Alan Gowans, and completed a doctorate at the University of Chicago (1988) under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Pramod Chandra. He curated at the British Museum (1994–2014).

Michael Witzel is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Karl Hoffmann, Paul Thieme, Hanns-Peter Schmidt, Johanna Narten, Jununath Pandit, and F. B. J. Kuiper. He held chairs of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1978–1986) and Harvard University (from 1986).

Michael Zimmermann is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hamburg (~1993–2000) and studied at Soka University. He held positions at Stanford University (2003) and Hamburg (~2007) as professor and director.

Michael von Brück is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his promotion at the University of Rostock (1968–1973) and studied at the University of Madras (~1980–1985). He held chairs at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and University of Munich (~1991–2014).

Michaela Haas works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2008), where she was supervised by Peter Schwieger, and also studied under Rechungpa and traditional teacher Jigme Namgyal Dzigar Kongtrul.

Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Komazawa University and earned her PhD from the University of Munich in 2014. She held positions at UC Berkeley and Stanford University, where she is Assistant Professor of Japanese Buddhism (attested 2017).

Michaël Peyrot is a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (1999–2010), later holding posts there (~2008, 2016) and at the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2014–2016).

Michel Bitbol is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Paris Diderot University under Pierre Mills (~1980–1985). He served as a CNRS research director (~1997) and held posts at Oxford, IHPST (~1997–2010), Paris 1, and the École Normale Supérieure (~2010).

Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, EPHE, and Collège de France (1864–1905), founding the Société de Linguistique de Paris in 1866.

Michel Clasquin-Johnson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at the University of South Africa from ~1989 through his doctoral thesis completion (~1994–1999), and joined the faculty there in 1990.

Michel Hulin is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1956) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1977) under Olivier Lacombe. He served as a faculty member at Paris-Sorbonne University from 1981 to 1998.
Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Boisselier (1988) and later served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1993–2008).

Michel Lejeune was a French linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1926–1929) and under Antoine Meillet (~1927–1932). He held academic posts at the University of Poitiers (~1937–1946), the University of Paris (~1947–1977), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1951–1977).

Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Geneva and studied under Seizan Yanagida. His posts include the University of Geneva (1987–1992), Hanazono University (attested 2000–2006), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (attested 2008–2012).

Michel Soymié was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at INALCO (~1948–1952) and held positions at the CNRS, EFEO, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he held a chair from ~1966 to 1992.

Michel Strickmann was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Leiden, the EPHE, and Paris Diderot (PhD ~1972–1979). He held positions at the University of Bordeaux (~1977–1978) and UC Berkeley (1978).
